title: Stepped-fidelity queue allocator with tenant weight decay for graceful degradation
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: During cross-region spikes and partial infra disruptions we've seen tenant requests either queue indefinitely or be dropped abruptly, causing customer-visible errors and SLO violations. Existing mechanisms (binary admission or single-tier priority queues) are too coarse: high-value tenants monopolize resources or low-value tenants get 100% rejections instead of useful degraded responses.

Proposal: Implement a stepped-fidelity queue allocator that maps incoming requests into a small number of resource-fidelity lanes (e.g., Full, Reduced, Cached/Stub). The allocator uses a per-tenant weight that decays over time to prevent burst monopolization. Admission is tokenized per-lane with dynamic replenishment tied to SLO consumption metrics (p99 latency, error budget burn). Integrate per-tenant circuit breakers to automatically move tenants to lower fidelity lanes if they repeatedly cause overloads. Support graceful degradation modes in-lane: context trimming, response compression, model downgrade (smaller model variant), and cached answer retrieval. The system must be region-aware: local-region lanes preferred, but in case of regional capacity pressure requests can be egressed to secondary regions with an attached stricter fidelity level.

Goals: reduce p99 latency SLO violations by 35% during overload windows, keep user-facing error rate <0.5% for production tier tenants under overload, provide meaningful degraded responses for at least 60% of requests that would otherwise be dropped.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator assigns requests to Full/Reduced/Cached lanes with metrics emitted per-lane
Per-tenant weight decay prevents long-running burst monopolies in 95% of simulated bursts
Circuit breaker transitions correctly per-tenant after 3 consecutive resource-threshold breaches
Region failover routes to secondary region with fidelity tag and shows no data leakage
Dashboards show lane-level SLOs and degradation counts; alerts fire when lane saturation crosses thresholds
End-to-end load test demonstrates >=35% reduction in p99 latency violations compared to baseline under identical traffic spike
implementation_steps: Design allocator state machine and size lanes (Full, Reduced, Cached) — design doc in Confluence: /confluence/rw/rl/stepped-fidelity-allocator
Add per-tenant weight meter with decay window (exponential decay 5m half-life) and eviction policy
Implement lane token buckets and dynamic replenishment based on real-time SLO consumption metrics
Integrate per-tenant circuit breaker (closed -> probing -> open) that reduces lane entitlement on open
Add region-aware routing hook to attach fidelity requirement and failover path
Implement graceful-degrade pipeline: context-trimmer, response-compressor, model-downgrade switch, cached-answer lookup
Instrument lane and tenant metrics, add dashboards and alert rules
Run synthetic chaos tests and staged canary with 5% traffic then 25% then 100%
Document runbooks and playbooks for on-call (how to revert, metric thresholds, mitigation steps)
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created after incident 2026-03-04 (region eu-west-1 partial GPU eviction) — initial triage complete (Asha)
2026-03-07: Design doc drafted, proposed lanes and exemplar degradation flows added. PM review requested (Ethan)
2026-03-09: Prototype allocator state machine implemented in staging; basic lane token buckets functional. First unit tests added (Ethan)
2026-03-12: Weight decay algorithm tuned to 5m half-life following synthetic burst tests; added metric labels for tenant_id and lane. Preparing PR for integration tests
decisions: Use 3 fidelity lanes (Full, Reduced, Cached) to balance complexity vs expressivity
Per-tenant weight decay chosen over strict quotas to allow short bursts but prevent monopolization
Circuit breaker thresholds set conservatively: open after 3 consecutive resource breaches or 10% error-rate increase in 1m window
Region failover prefers 'reduced' fidelity in secondary region to limit cross-region cost and tail latency
open_risks: Edge case where Reduced lane still causes queueing if many tenants downgrade simultaneously — needs cross-tenant pacing
Cached/stub lane requires robust cache invalidation strategy for freshness-sensitive endpoints
Model-downgrade step may change output schema/format causing client regressions — needs compatibility shim
Observability cost: lane-level cardinality growth for tenant_id may increase metrics storage costs
testing_plan: Unit tests for weight decay math and token-bucket replenishment
Integration tests: multi-tenant synthetic traffic with mixed request sizes to validate fair-share
Chaos test: kill 50% of local-region serving nodes and verify failover fidelity tags and degraded response rates
Canary rollout: enable allocator for 5% of traffic, monitor lane saturation and SLO deviations, then 25%
Production validation: two-week observation window with circuit-breaker telemetry and customer impact review
runbook_extracts: If Full lane saturation > 85% for >3m: escalate to on-call, temporarily increase Reduced lane tokens by 20% if error budget allows
If tenant circuit-breaker opens: notify tenant owner, log incident, and enable auto-probe after 10m
If cross-region egress increases >5x baseline: trigger cost review and consider temporary regional scaling
